architecture: Three shipped modules plus one outer project repo, split on the licence/lifecycle boundary rather than on the technical one. **Channel split:** (a) Babele 2.9.1 owns all compendium content — all three packs are single-Adventure packs, 2,703,509 raw chars; (b) Foundry native i18n owns the system's 590 UI keys plus the plugins' lang files; (c) a runtime patcher module owns the ~115 sites neither channel can reach (80 system template literals, ~33 module-JS literals, the plugins' hardcoded strings, and Handlebars-partial pre-registration for `terminal` and `motion-tracker-multideck`). **The system's lang/cn.json is overridden, not forked — confirmed in source, not assumed.** `Localization#getTranslations` (foundry.mjs:204905-204942) builds one flat dictionary by pushing translation files in a fixed order — core (`CORE_SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES` is `["en"]` only, foundry.mjs:3513, so `cn` comes entirely from packages) → **game.system** → **every active module, in module order** → world — then `for (const p of promises) mergeObject(translations, json, {inplace:true})`, so **later wins and a module's `lang/cn.json` overwrites the system's key-for-key**; `#filterLanguagePaths` (204953) honours a per-entry `"system"` / `"module"` gate (`checkSystem`/`checkModule`), and `#loadTranslationFile` runs `expandObject` on every file so flat-dotted or nested JSON both resolve. That gate is what lets ONE module carry the system override *and* companion lang files for `alien-mu-th-ur` / `motion_tracker` / `token-action-hud-alien` at zero cost when those aren't installed. **Module 1 `alienrpg-cn`** is the always-present hub: the system lang override, the runtime patcher, CJK CSS, the *single* global `babele.registerMapping()` layer (it is a global layer — registering it from three modules would triple-merge), and the 76k-char system Adventure pack. **Module 2 `alien-evolved-starterset-cn`** and **Module 3 `alien-evolved-corerules-cn`** each carry only `compendium/{cn,en}/` plus a five-line `babele.register({module, lang:'cn', dir})` esmodule and `requires: [babele, alienrpg-cn]`. They are separate because `alien-evolved-corerules` is `"protected": true` — paid Free League content — and its 2.29M translated chars must be publishable, withholdable, and versioned independently of everything else. Lang code is `cn` throughout (the system, TAH-core and 13 installed modules use `cn`; only 2 use `zh-CN`), and the plugin lang entries are gated with `"module"` so a `cn` world without them loads nothing extra.

phase_plan.work: Release alienrpg-cn and alien-evolved-starterset-cn per the EC process: version + download + changelog all three edited in module.json, tag shape matching what release.yml literally verifies, `rm -f module.zip` before `zip -r` (appending to a stale zip once shipped 22MB of corrupted content to users), per-repo -x exclusion list copied FROM THAT REPO'S OWN release.yml (compendium/en/*, lang/en.json, lang_keep_english.json, .github/*, *.zip — but NOT scripts/, which ships here because the runtime patchers are esmodules). Post-release: download the artifact, `unzip -Z1` (never `unzip -l`) and assert the exclusions held. Append a chronology row AT RELEASE TIME. Open a PR to pwatson100/alienrpg with the subset of lang/cn.json that maps 1:1 onto en.json's 590 keys — he has accepted translations from four outside contributors and issue #282 says 'just open a PR'. Also file the `systems/alienrpglates/...` ActiveEffect sheet-path typo and the NBSP mismatch in welcomeJournalEntry as upstream bugs. Rewrite PROJECT.md §1/§6/§7 from actual measurement (git status + git log -1), never transcription. Corerules-cn release decision deferred to the licensing answer.
phase_plan.exit_criteria: Both public modules install from their manifest URL into a clean Foundry and render Chinese end-to-end; published zips verified member-by-member; chronology rows appended in the same commit as the tags; the upstream PR is open with a link recorded in §6; PROJECT.md §7 smoke-test checklist reflects what was actually run this round, and the §1 blind-spot table names at least three error classes that still have no criterion.

open_questions.question: Is the Alien stack deployed to the same VPS as the Crucible/Ember work, or is it local?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Your memory carries a standing rule — 汉化装在 VPS；本地安装状态不能当诊断证据，已栽两次 — but the Alien evidence points the other way: this machine has alienrpg 4.1.13, all six companion modules, Babele 2.9.1 and foundry_chn installed, and the three packs are already dumped from local LevelDB. Every phase exit above depends on a real smoke test, and smoke testing is the single item the Ember/Crucible project never once closed across every release. If play happens on the VPS and I test locally, I will be repeating exactly the mistake the rule exists to prevent — and three of the top risks here (the name-lookup import traps, the crit-injury parse, the enum/derived-field class) are ONLY visible with Foundry actually loaded.
open_questions.options: (a) Local is the deployment — test here, no VPS involvement. (b) VPS is the deployment, local is a scratch rig — then PROJECT.md §2 must state the VPS's installed versions as the authority and every 'verified in a world' claim must name which world. (c) Both — VPS for play, local as the designated smoke rig, with a documented version-parity check before each release.
open_questions.recommendation: (c). Keep the local install as the smoke rig because it already has all seven packages, but write the VPS's package versions into PROJECT.md §2 as the release authority and add a one-line parity assertion to the pre-release block. Say which it is before Phase 0 finishes — this choice determines what 'verified' means for the rest of the project.

open_questions.question: One module or one per package?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the licence boundary, not just a packaging preference. alien-evolved-corerules is `"protected": true` — paid content served from Free League's S3 manifest — while alien-evolved-starterset is `"protected": false` and the system is open source. A single module would force everyone to download 2.29M chars of translated premium text and would make it impossible to withhold that one piece if the licensing answer comes back badly.
open_questions.options: (a) One module for everything. (b) Three: alienrpg-cn hub + starterset-cn + corerules-cn. (c) Five: split the six companion plugins out of the hub into their own module too.
open_questions.recommendation: (b), with the plugins folded into the hub. The plugin surfaces are tiny (3.5k + 9.2k + 2.2k + ~1.6k + 14 chars) and Foundry's per-entry `"module"` gate in #filterLanguagePaths means they cost literally nothing when the target module is absent — I verified that gate in foundry.mjs:204953. Splitting them would triple the release overhead for ~16k chars. The one argument for (c) is that `terminal` is a generic sci-fi module used outside Alien, so a Chinese terminal translation has standalone value; if you want that, split only `terminal`.

open_questions.question: Bilingual 「中文 (English)」 names like the PF2E project, or Chinese-only?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Alien cannot take one uniform answer, because three separate code paths compare names with `===`. A blanket bilingual rule would break the 12 skill-stunts lookups; a blanket Chinese-only rule would break the same 12 plus the 9 first-run import lookups; and the physical Free League book is English-only, so players cross-referencing page numbers need the English somewhere.
open_questions.options: (a) Bilingual everywhere. (b) Chinese-only everywhere. (c) Three tiers: FROZEN ENGLISH for the 9 import-lookup names + 11 hard-coded RollTable names + 2 folder names + 'PACK MULE'/'TAKE CONTROL'/'None'; EXACT-MATCH CHINESE for the 12 skill-stunts item names (must equal lang/cn.json's ALIENRPG.Skill<key> byte-for-byte, no English tail); BILINGUAL 「中文 English」 on name and page-name fields for proper nouns, gear, talents, planets and tables; bare Chinese in prose and inside {labels}.
open_questions.recommendation: (c). It is the only option that satisfies all three code paths, and it matches the Ember/Crucible convention you already have tooling for (build_glossary keys on (English, FIELD ROLE) precisely because 'does this name carry the English tail' is a per-field decision). One sub-choice for you: the separator — the Crucible project uses a space, the PF2E work uses parentheses. I recommend a plain space so residue.py's Latin-word scan stays simple.

open_questions.question: 异形 or 异型?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the single most repeated noun in the corpus and it seeds the glossary base layer.
open_questions.recommendation: 异形, and this one is effectively settled rather than open. The four-film subtitle corpus (4,601 aligned bilingual pairs) has 56 occurrences of 异形 and ZERO of 异型; zh.wikipedia's article title, the 异形系列 page and the 2024 mainland theatrical release 《异形：夺命舰》 all use 异形; and the system's own cn.json already uses it (ALIENRPG.DialTextXeno, ALIENRPG.MenuLabel). Also encode the ZH split the subtitles make and English does not: 异形 = the creature, 外星 = the adjective (外星船 'alien ship'), so the pipeline never renders 'alien ship' as 异形船.

open_questions.question: Contribute lang/cn.json upstream to pwatson100/alienrpg, or override it in our module?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The upstream file is not merely incomplete, it is actively wrong in ~107 keys with 40 documented hard errors, and it is byte-identical between your install and master, so nothing newer exists to pull. Whichever way you go, other Chinese-speaking Alien GMs get the current broken file by default.
open_questions.options: (a) Override only — fastest, no permission needed, and it is the only route for the 35 keys that don't exist in en.json and the `alienrpgct` namespace. (b) Upstream only — one file for everyone, but we wait on a maintainer and lose the extra keys. (c) Both.
open_questions.recommendation: (c). Ship the override first (Phase 1) so you are never blocked, then upstream the subset that maps 1:1 onto en.json's 590 keys once it has survived a release. Upstream is receptive — Paul Watson has merged translations from at least four outside contributors and issue #282's answer to 'how do I start translating' was 'just open a PR'. If he merges, our override becomes a harmless no-op for those keys and still wins the merge, so there is no conflict state to manage. Bundle the two upstream BUGS with it: the `systems/alienrpglates/...` sheet-path typo that breaks the ActiveEffect config, and the NBSP mismatch that makes `game.journal.getName(welcomeJournalEntry)` return undefined.

open_questions.question: Is shipping a Chinese translation of alien-evolved-corerules (`"protected": true`) a redistribution problem?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the highest-severity decision in the project and it governs 2,286,505 of the 2,703,509 chars — 85% of the work. The module is flagged protected, meaning paid content behind Free League's own manifest; the translation is a derivative work of the full text of a book that is itself a 20th Century Studios sublicence; and Free League has licensed exactly seven Alien RPG languages (French, German, Spanish, Italian, Russian, Polish, Portuguese) with named partners — Chinese is not among them, and Alien is not in Free League's third-party/OGL programme at all.
open_questions.options: (a) Build it and keep the repo private; distribute only to people who already own the pack, via a manifest they configure themselves. (b) Publish it publicly and accept the risk. (c) Don't build it — stop after Phase 4. (d) Ask Free League (and/or Paul Watson, who maintains the module) for permission before Phase 5 starts.
open_questions.recommendation: (a) + (d), started NOW rather than at Phase 5. Send the enquiry during Phase 0 — it costs nothing, the answer takes weeks, and it arrives before you have spent ~1.95M chars of translation effort on something you may not be able to ship. Meanwhile: build corerules-cn in a private repo from day one, never publish its manifest, and make sure `compendium/en/*` is in the zip exclusion list for every repo (it is the upstream English text verbatim — shipping it converts a translation overlay into an unambiguous redistribution of the book). Note the exposure is not binary: the starterset is `protected: false` but still Free League IP, and even the system's lang/cn.json contains the Panic Table entries verbatim — though upstreaming those is the safest possible home for them, since upstream already ships that text in English and Chinese.

open_questions.question: How far do we go on the critical-injury tables, given the hard-coded parse at actor.mjs:1888-1941?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The crit tables are among the most-read content in Alien, and the system parses their result TEXT by splitting it and string-comparing columns against localize('ALIENRPG.Yes'/'None'/'OneRound'/'OneTurn'/'OneShift'/'OneDay'/'Permanent') plus a bare literal 'Shift' that has no i18n key at all. The current cn.json already half-translated that set, so healTime silently resolves to 0 on Chinese play today. Two of the source cases use EN DASH U+2013, not ASCII hyphen — a transcription error there produces cases that can never match.
open_questions.options: (a) Leave the crit tables in English. (b) Translate the prose but keep the machine-parsed columns byte-identical English (rows read Chinese with English 'Permanent'/'One Shift' fragments). (c) Translate tables and the 8 lang keys in exact lockstep, pinned by an assertion, and add a runtime patch for the un-keyed 'Shift' literal.
open_questions.recommendation: (c), with scan_crit_lockstep.py as a standing gate and the healTime check on the Phase-1 smoke list. (b) is the safe fallback if the smoke test fails. Do not choose (a) — the Panic and Critical Injury tables are the tables players actually read at the table.

open_questions.question: Wiki-formal or player-colloquial register for the franchise nouns?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The two registers disagree on the most visible nouns and you cannot satisfy both. zh.wikipedia says 抱脸体 / 破胸体 / 韦兰-尤坦尼集团 / 诺史莫号; the mainland fan corpus (百度百科, 萌娘百科, bilibili, 机核, douban) says 抱脸虫 / 破胸者 / 维兰德-汤谷公司 / 诺斯托罗莫号. The only Weyland-Yutani rendering attested anywhere in your subtitle corpus is 伟伦优达尼 — a Taiwan-flavoured phonetic that neither camp uses, and it appears exactly twice.
open_questions.options: (a) Wiki-formal throughout (defensible, citable, matches the term-priority ladder's wiki-first rule). (b) Player-colloquial throughout (matches what a Chinese Alien player will actually say at the table). (c) Wiki-formal for the glossary spine, colloquial as a documented alias in glossary_alien.disputes.json.
open_questions.recommendation: (a) as the spine with (c)'s alias file, because your own term-priority ladder puts wiki above everything — but with one deliberate exception: 抱脸虫 over 抱脸体 for Facehugger, since it is overwhelmingly dominant in mainland usage and 虫 reads correctly for a creature while 体 reads like a specimen label. Note that all four films come from ONE fansub lineage (CnSCG), so cross-film 'agreement' in the subtitle corpus is an artifact, not four independent votes — weight it as a single source. Also flag: 伟伦优达尼 should be treated as weak evidence and NOT adopted.

risks: LICENSING / REDISTRIBUTION — the top risk, governing 85% of the work. alien-evolved-corerules declares "protected": true and ships from Free League's own S3 manifest (url frialigan.se), i.e. it is paid content. A Chinese translation of its 2,286,505 chars is a derivative of the full text of a book that is itself a 20th Century Studios sublicence. Free League has licensed exactly seven Alien RPG languages, none of them Chinese, and Alien is excluded from their third-party/OGL programme. Mitigations that must be in place from Phase 0, not Phase 5: corerules-cn lives in a private repo; compendium/en/* is in every repo's zip exclusion list (shipping it turns an overlay into verbatim redistribution of the English book); the licensing enquiry goes out at the START, not after the effort is spent. The starterset (protected:false) is lower exposure but not zero.

NINE ENGLISH-NAME LOOKUP TRAPS BREAK FIRST-RUN IMPORT — a class the survey never captured, and worse than the RollTable traps it did. All three packages do unguarded === lookups: adventurePackName ('Alien RPG System' / 'Alien Evolved Core Rules' / 'Alien Evolved Starter Set'), welcomeJournalEntry ('MU/TH/ER Instructions.' / 'CORE RULES - HOW TO USE THIS MODULE' / 'STARTER SET - HOW TO USE THIS MODULE') and sceneToActivate ('Alien Evolved Core Rules' / 'Alien Evolved Starter Set'). They are read via pack.getName(...).sheet._updateObject (init.mjs:77, corerules init.js:82, starterset init.js:115) and game.journal.getName(...).show() / game.scenes.getName(...).activate() with no null check, and via pack.index.find(a => a.name === ...). Babele translates the index in place (babele-runtime-applier.js:33 translateIndex(pack.index)), so translating any of these nine produces an unguarded TypeError on first import, not a silent degradation. They must be frozen English AND gated by a script — a bilingual name will not work, the comparison is strict equality.

CRIT-INJURY LOCKSTEP PARSE. actor.mjs:1888-1941 splits crit-table result text and compares columns against 7 localized keys plus the bare literal 'Shift' that has no i18n key at all. The current cn.json already half-translated that set, so healTime resolves to 0 on Chinese play today. Two cases use EN DASH U+2013 (', –1 ', ', –2 '), not ASCII hyphen — the survey transcribed them as ASCII, and anyone building the lockstep from that transcription produces cases that can never match. Needs a runtime-verified smoke test, not a static check.

SCALE AND QUOTA. ~2.4M net-new chars over 8-10 parallel waves at 270-310k EN chars each. The wave scratchpad is session-scoped ($env:ALIEN_PARALLEL_ROOT) and runIds are session-local, so anything unlanded at a session boundary is lost. Adversarial review is always what the quota kills — translators run first and eat the window — so 'batches are complete' will keep reading as 'this wave is done' when it is not. Land and commit every batch before switching sessions, and confirm review actually ran from disk, never from the workflow return value (two EC runs reported agents_error 13 / agents_done 0 while actually advancing 219 then 422 of 493 pages).

NO OLD BASELINE EXISTS YET, AND UPSTREAM CAN MOVE SILENTLY. Until Phase 0's capture_baseline lands, every drift criterion degrades to a length heuristic. Both content modules ship a `-latest.json` manifest on an S3 bucket, so alien-evolved-corerules/starterset 1.0.2 can be replaced under us with no version pin to notice it. Snapshot all three packs FULLY on every catch-up round — the EC project snapshotted 3 of 10 packs and three drift gates ran on 30% of the corpus for months while printing clean reports.

THRESHOLD CONSTANTS DO NOT TRANSFER. EC's 0.31 CN/EN median, 0.22 TRUNCATED and 0.25 catch-up floor are corpus-specific, and this corpus is far more extreme: journal visible-text ratios run 42% (corerules) to 77% (system) of raw, with individual pages at 13-16% (CR-J-14b is 59,662 raw / 8,438 visible). A ratio wired from EC's numbers would flag most correct translations. measure_ratio.py must run on TAG-STRIPPED text and emit per-document-class bands before any threshold is wired — and remember EC's own lesson that one known blocking defect sat at 0.377, squarely inside the normal band, so ratio is a candidate filter and never a verdict.

BABELE GLOBAL-LAYER POLLUTION. registerMapping pushes a GLOBAL layer merged into every Babele-managed pack. The survey's proposed mapping guards only the `description` variants with `exists`; every other variant (notes on type 'character'/'creature', weaponClass on 'weapon', capacity, appearance, adhocItems…) fires unguarded on other systems' documents. 'character', 'creature' and 'weapon' are among the most common type keys in Foundry, so a dnd5e or pf2e export would gain alien-only keys. Translate-time is fail-open, but export pollution is real. Guard every variant. Same class: Adventure.items/tables expose:true is also global and changes behaviour for every third-party adventure pack in the world.

BABELE'S OWN importAdventure HOOK OVERWRITES TOKEN NAMES. babele.js:52-70 registers an importAdventure hook, and the world setting syncImportedAdventureTokenNames (settings.js:62-72, default TRUE) rewrites placed Scene token names from the imported Actor's prototypeToken.name AFTER creation — which would overwrite anything a Scene.tokens nameCollection mapping wrote. Moot today (0 tokens across all 15 scenes) but it is the direct context for the tokenName decision, and the survey never mentions it. This is one reason to drop the proposed alienTokenName converter rather than keep it.

LANG OVERRIDE CANNOT DELETE, ONLY OVERWRITE. mergeObject merges later-over-earlier but has no deletion semantics, so the 14 dead pre-v11 ACTOR.Type*/ITEM.Type* orphan keys and the JSON-null ALIENRPG.EVCriticalInjuries persist from the system's file unless we write a value over them. For EVCriticalInjuries specifically the correct action is to write NOTHING: localize() falls through to the English fallback dictionary and returns 'EV - Critical Injuries', which is exactly what game.tables.getName needs — adding a Chinese value there would BREAK the lookup.

UPSTREAM BUGS THAT WILL LOOK LIKE OURS. active-effect-config.mjs:21/24 point at `systems/alienrpglates/sheets/active-effect/...` — a system id that does not exist and a path that does not exist, so the ActiveEffect config sheet is already broken and its three templates (and the 6 DRAW_STEEL.* leftovers inside them) are unreachable dead surface. Do not spend effort translating them and do not add a DRAW_STEEL block. Likewise the NBSP mismatch between init.js's welcomeJournalEntry and the pack's journal name means getName already returns undefined. File both upstream so a future round does not mistake them for translation damage.

CJK RENDERING DEFECTS IN THE PLUGINS, TWO OF THEM REAL BUGS. terminal.js:1146-1165 pads monospace table columns with padEnd on String.length — double-width CJK ragged the '|' borders of help/ls/ssh output; terminal.js:877's gsap scrambleText chars pool is Latin-only, so Chinese scrambles into lowercase ASCII and changes width mid-animation on 20 of 28 shipped styles; terminal.js:1216 has a keydown Enter handler with no isComposing guard (IME-unsafe). MU-TH-UR sets 46 inline `font-family: monospace` via style.cssText, so only an injected stylesheet with !important can override. None of these is fixable from a lang file.

THE 12 SKILL-STUNTS ITEM NAMES ARE A LOOKUP KEY BOUND TO lang/cn.json. character-skills.hbs:15 emits data-pmbut='{{skill.description}}', system.skills.<skl>.description is overwritten every prepareDerivedData from game.i18n.localize('ALIENRPG.Skill<key>'), and character-sheet.mjs:1119 does game.items.getName(dataset.pmbut). So the pack items and the lang file are coupled across two modules and two phases: changing a skill translation in Phase 1 silently breaks 12 stunts popovers translated in Phase 2. Needs a standing assertion, not a comment.

TERM CORPUS IS ONE VOTE, NOT FOUR. All four film subtitle files are CnSCG (圣城家园) releases from a single translation lineage, so cross-film 'consistency' is an artifact of shared provenance. Several renderings are Taiwan-flavoured (士官长, 太空梭, 电波枪, 复仇161星, 伟伦优达尼) and several are outright wrong (APC→焚化炉, dropship erased, stasis→静态平衡, Ellen→海伦). The corpus also has ZERO attestation for Facehugger, Chestburster, Ovomorph, Drone, Warrior, USCSS, Acheron, Hadley's Hope, MU/TH/UR-as-spelled, or the number in Special Order 937 — precisely the RPG vocabulary. Treat it as one weak source under the wiki, never as consensus.

SMOKE TESTING IS THE FAILURE MODE MOST LIKELY TO REPEAT. The Ember/Crucible project shipped every single version without it and says so in its own document. Here at least five defect classes are invisible to every static check: the nine import-name traps, the crit healTime parse, enum-shaped fields translated as prose (which breaks runtime and throws console errors while every JSON comparison stays green), the expose:true embedded-item inheritance, and whether Foundry's TOC builder honours explicit heading ids so #anchor links still jump. Each phase's exit criteria above names a live-world check for exactly this reason — if a phase ships without it, the phase is not done.
corrections_applied: MAPPING BUG: the Item variant `_when {path:'type', equals:'crit-inj'}` is dead — `crit-inj` is a filename, the registered type is `critical-injury` (alienrpg.mjs:144, system.json documentTypes.Item, item-sheet.mjs:124). Corrected in mappings.mjs; the forward-compat mapping it claimed to provide did not exist.

DROPPED the proposed `alienTokenName` converter entirely. Babele's built-in `name` converter (Converters.mappedField('name')) has no .extract, so it emits no key; alienTokenName.extract would inject 74 redundant tokenName keys (~1.8k chars) into every actor entry for zero translate-time benefit, since prototypeToken.name === name for 74/74 actors. It also collides with Babele's importAdventure/syncImportedAdventureTokenNames hook, which rewrites token names post-import anyway.

GUARD POLICY EXTENDED: `exists` guards go on EVERY variant field, not only the ones redefining `description`. registerMapping pushes a global layer (document-mappings.js:267-287) and 'character'/'creature'/'weapon' are common type keys across systems, so the unguarded notes/weaponClass/capacity/appearance/adhocItems/signatureItem/relationship variants would leak alien-only keys into other systems' exports.

system.modifiers.*.label/.ability stay DO-NOT-TRANSLATE, but on one leg not two: no registered Item type inherits base-item's prepareDerivedData (all 13 override it) and `feature` is not a registered type at all, so the 'derived' justification is false. The surviving reason is that templates/item/item-modifiers.hbs never renders them (it emits {{localize 'ALIENRPG.*'}} instead).

system.header.type.value is NOT a '0'/'1' enum. Measured across the three packs it holds '1'–'9' on item/weapon/spacecraftweapons; the cited '0'/'1' switch in actor-spacecraft.mjs is guarded by `type === 'spacecraft-crit'` and there are zero such items. Real readers are item-modifiers.hbs:2/:50 and item-sheet.mjs:236/239/242. Verdict unchanged, reasoning replaced.

system.general.sigItem.value / relOne.value / relTwo.value are NOT all 'None' — sigItem holds real content ('Toy dinosaur', 'Company ID badge', 'Cross necklace') and relOne/relTwo hold CHARACTER NAMES ('MacWhirr', 'Hirsch', 'Sigg', 'Singleton'). Added a cross-reference hazard the survey never raised: those two fields must stay in sync with the translated Actor names or the pregen relationship lines point at people who no longer exist. Only system.general.agenda.value is genuinely all-'None'.

JOURNAL LINK SYNTAX CORRECTED: the packs use `@UUID[Item.<id>]{label}` (v10+ form), not `@Item[...]` / `@JournalEntry[...]`. Every QA regex, translator guard and BRIEF.md markup table targets @UUID; a rule written against the survey's stated shape would match zero occurrences and pass a file where every link was destroyed.

ADDED 36 RollTable draw-enrichers to the table-name sync surface: 33 `@TEXTDRAW[RollTable.<id>]{label}` + 3 `@DRAW[RollTable.<id>]{label}`, all in corerules journal prose, 32 distinct labels of which 25 match a pack RollTable name byte-for-byte and 7 differ only by NBSP. The survey devoted a whole risk entry to keeping table names in sync and then missed the second place they are written down. This is why scan_table_ref_sync.py checks four writing sites, not two.

42 embedded items DO share an _id with an adventure-level item in the same pack (38 corerules, 4 starterset), contradicting 'no _id collisions exist'. They happen to be same-name so the safety conclusion holds, but Babele's default Item match order is _id-FIRST (document-identity.js:3-6), so for those 42 the lookup is not name-keyed at all.

Of the 25 embedded items not covered by expose:true, five (Pilot, Roughneck, Officer, Colonial Marine, Scientist — all type `specialty`) exist only in the SYSTEM pack, not the core pack, and two (Weyland-Yutani Key Card, Kitchen Knife) exist in no pack. That changes the remediation: five are inheritable by pointing the starterset file's Item block at the system pack.

Scene notes carrying entryId+pageId: 25 of 37, not 33. The other 12 map pins are free-standing labels with no journal backing, so the 'translate both consistently' rule applies to fewer pins and the remaining 12 are standalone strings.

Folder inventory: 31 distinct names, not 26. The shared-_id set (an import-order hazard the survey itself flagged) omitted three — 'Alien Macros', 'Alien RPG Mother Aids', 'The Art of Alien' — and 'Alien Evolved' occurs 5×, not 3×.

ALIENRPG.EVCriticalInjuries is present-as-JSON-null, not missing, and the stated failure mechanism is inverted. Localization#localize falls through to the English _fallback dictionary before returning the raw key, so it returns 'EV - Critical Injuries' and game.tables.getName already succeeds. The practical conclusion (leave that table English) is unchanged, but the corollary is the opposite of what the survey implies: adding a Chinese value for that key would BREAK the lookup. Written into lang_keep_english.json as a do-not-fill entry.

REMOVED the DRAW_STEEL work item. The three templates/active-effect/*.hbs files are unreachable — active-effect-config.mjs:21/24 point at `systems/alienrpglates/sheets/active-effect/...`, a system id that does not exist and a path that does not exist (a botched find-and-replace). Nothing renders as a raw key there and a DRAW_STEEL block in cn.json is wasted work. Reclassified as an upstream bug to file. The 6 EFFECT.* keys likewise never render from this system.

ADDED the `alienrpgct` namespace: `alienrpgct.Passive` and `alienrpgct.Inactive` (helpers/effects.mjs:15/20) render as literal dotted keys as the Passive/Inactive headers on the Item sheet's effects tab. The namespace exists in NO lang file of any package. The survey listed the ALIENRPG.Effect.Temporary sibling one line above and missed these two because its key regex only matched the ALIENRPG/TYPES/ACTOR/ITEM prefixes.

SCOPE WIDENED: module/ contains 12 .js files (5,428 lines) besides the 62 .mjs, and two are live in the import graph with user-visible English — devmsg.js:24 sets a ChatMessage `alias: "Alien RPG News"` (a permanently visible English byline on the GM's ready-time whisper) and apps/update.js:146-153 builds a Dialog with an English title/content/'Okay!' label. Both added to the runtime-patch table.

CRIT-PARSE BYTES CORRECTED: actor.mjs:1906/1912 use EN DASH U+2013 in `", –1 "` / `", –2 "`, not ASCII hyphen-minus. The ALIENRPG.None case is at actor.mjs:1924 (switch spans 1922-1941), not :1955. In the survey's own 'MOST IMPORTANT' finding the literal bytes are the entire deliverable.
Markup-bearing lang values: 26, not 34. The zero-tag-loss conclusion reproduces and stands.

Referenced-key census restated as approximate rather than verified: an independent scan of the live import graph plus all 101 templates gives 487 distinct keys, 94 byte-identical-to-en, 162 rendering English, 35 referenced-but-absent-from-en — against the survey's 494 / 98 / 166 / 34. Only the 68-missing figure reproduces exactly. Direction and magnitude (~33%) are right; the specific numbers are not quotable.
